headline: Low interaction risk: both profiles are non-runnable, network-egress-none reference lists, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked by design.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent is runnable, and both profiles expose no I/O surfaces or shared channel. Agent A is an open-source reference list with network_egress none; agent B is also network_egress none and has empty io_surfaces. No pathway exists for one to inject instructions into the other by default.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent becomes runnable and parses the other's text as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents non-runnable in the current deployment.
Do not add shared clipboard or filesystem mounts.
Avoid piping outputs from one agent directly into the other.
Review any future MCP or queue integration before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The pair touches no data classes, has no I/O surfaces, and both profiles state network_egress none. Agent A and agent B are documentation-style repositories rather than data-processing services, so there is no plausible default leakage path between them.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent begins uploading file contents or logs to a backend, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Confirm both agents remain local-only with no egress.
Disable automatic log export if added later.
Separate any future workspaces by project.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. Agent A has no permissions_requested and agent B has empty concurrency_model and sandboxing fields, while both are non-runnable reference assets. Without writable shared resources, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk must be reconsidered.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared mutable state, the pathway may emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not grant shared filesystem write permissions.
Avoid placing them in the same mutable git workspace.
Add locking before any future shared-state integration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B has no documented action-taking authority, and agent A is a static reference list rather than a fact-producing service. Since neither profile shows a pipeline where B treats A's output as authoritative, there is no default cascading-error pathway.
conditions: IF B is later configured to consume A's outputs as authoritative input, reassess.
IF either agent is connected to downstream actions such as email, commits, or tickets, the risk changes.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action.
Do not auto-ingest A's outputs into B.
Keep both agents in advisory-only roles.
Add verification steps if a workflow is introduced later.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched, no residency or retention fields indicate regulated data flow, and both agents are open-source reference lists. Because the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or other regulated data handling, there is no compliance mismatch to score.
conditions: IF either agent is later used to process regulated data, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency, retention, or certification fields are added, the assessment may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both workflows.
Document any future residency or retention requirements.
Review compliance before adding customer data.
Use separate environments for regulated workloads.
